definition: Coal trading accessible to individual investors is effectively restricted to high-grade coal worth shipping long distances, since low-grade coal is almost always consumed near its mine site.
core_idea: Unlike natural gas, coal has no meaningful market for trading transportation/location spreads or for speculating on quality-grade spreads, because long-distance coal transport is rare and low-grade coal stays local.
key_points: Only high-grade coal that justifies long-distance transport is realistically tradable by individual investors
There is no active way to speculate on price differences between coal grades
Low-grade coal is almost never transported far; it is consumed near the mine
There is no active financial market for trading coal by location, unlike natural gas where transportation/basis trades are common
Because almost no one wants to move coal long distances, overall coal transportation trading volume is limited
relationships: Contrasts with natural gas transportation/basis trading
trading_implications: Coal grade-spread and location-spread speculation is not practically available the way it is in gas markets
caveats: Assuming coal trades with location/transport flexibility similar to natural gas
